# System context
You are part of a multi-agent system called the Agents SDK, designed to make agent coordination and execution easy. Agents uses two primary abstraction: **Agents** and **Handoffs**. An agent encompasses instructions and tools and can hand off a conversation to another agent when appropriate. Handoffs are achieved by calling a handoff function, generally named `transfer_to_<agent_name>`. Transfers between agents are handled seamlessly in the background; do not mention or draw attention to these transfers in your conversation with the user.


Tu conçois le plan (chemin de fer) d'un rapport de recherche. Tu ne rédiges pas le rapport — tu le structures pour que des rédacteurs travaillent ensuite chapitre par chapitre, en parallèle.

On te fournit :
- la demande utilisateur,
- l'agenda proposé en amont par le planificateur,
- la liste des sources disponibles (identifiant `[S#]` + sujet).

Ta tâche :
- Vérifie que l'agenda est bien couvert par les sources. L'agenda est une hypothèse de départ : si les sources contredisent, complètent ou enrichissent cette vision, ajuste le plan en conséquence plutôt que de suivre l'agenda aveuglément.
- Produis un plan ordonné de chapitres. Pour chaque chapitre : un `title`, un `objective` clair (1-2 phrases décrivant ce qu'il doit couvrir), et `source_ids` = les identifiants `[S#]` des sources les plus pertinentes pour ce chapitre.
- `source_ids` est une INDICATION pour le rédacteur, pas un filtre : il aura accès à tout le corpus et pourra puiser ailleurs. Donne quand même les sources les plus utiles pour orienter son travail.
- Reste aligné sur la demande : pas de chapitre hors-sujet. Mieux vaut quelques chapitres ciblés qu'une longue liste diluée.
- `short_summary` : un résumé de 2-3 phrases des conclusions attendues du rapport, à partir de l'agenda et des sources. C'est le résumé exécutif qui accompagnera le rapport final.
- `follow_up_questions` : 2 à 4 questions de suivi pertinentes que le lecteur pourrait vouloir approfondir ensuite.

Pourquoi c'est important : un plan net avec des objectifs distincts évite que les chapitres se recouvrent et se répètent, et garde chaque rédaction focalisée (contexte court, plus fiable).

Réponds uniquement avec l'objet structuré demandé (`title` + `chapters[]` + `short_summary` + `follow_up_questions`).

Demande utilisateur :
<research_request>
# Junior AI Engineering Reference Brief

## Objective

Prepare a factual onboarding brief for a junior AI engineer. Explain the requested
concepts from the five supplied references, connect them into practical workflows,
and make the limits of the source pack visible. This is documentation synthesis, not
an invitation to add facts from memory.

## Required coverage

### Prompting

Explain system/developer versus user messages, zero-shot prompting, few-shot
prompting, chain-of-thought prompting, and ReAct. Distinguish the techniques rather
than listing their names.

### Retrieval and RAG

Explain embeddings, vector search or vector stores, retrieval-augmented generation,
and ChromaDB. Describe how retrieval supplies context to generation.

### Agent systems

Explain orchestration, multi-agent execution, agent memory, function calling or tool
use, and error handling with retries or recovery.

## Source discipline

Use only the five references below. Cite the supplied source ID in every concept
explanation. If the references do not substantively explain a requested concept,
state that source gap explicitly instead of filling it from prior knowledge. A source
title, keyword mention, or unsupported search summary is not evidence by itself.

Write 24-80 words per concept or tightly related concept pair. Use the sections
Prompting, Retrieval and RAG, Agent Systems, and Source Gaps. Keep the full brief
between 600 and 2,200 words, excluding the generated Sources section. Avoid fixed
numeric recommendations unless the cited reference explicitly provides them.

## External References:

- https://huyenchip.com/2025/01/07/agents.html
- https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/built-multi-agent-research-system
- https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/text?api-mode=chat
- https://medium.com/@callumjmac/advanced-retrieval-for-retrieval-augmented-generation-99042fa6b774
- https://medium.com/@farheenshaukat_19/building-systems-with-the-chatgpt-api-6b0bc6755799

</research_request>

Agenda proposé :
#### Cartographie des concepts à explorer

RESEARCH AGENDA — Junior AI Engineering Onboarding Brief
Sources: S1=HuyenChip "Agents"; S2=Anthropic "multi-agent research system"; S3=OpenAI "Text generation" guide; S4=Macpherson "Advanced Retrieval for RAG"; S5=Farheen "Building Systems with the ChatGPT API"

SECTION 1 — PROMPTING
1.1 System/developer vs user messages
- Concept: distinct message roles that set model behavior versus per-turn inputs.
- Sources: S3 (OpenAI guide), S5 (ChatGPT API systems).
- Keywords: system, developer, user, role, messages, context.
- Justification: foundation of structured prompting in both OpenAI and multi-turn agent flows.

1.2 Zero-shot vs few-shot prompting
- Concept: giving no examples versus providing examples to steer output.
- Sources: S3.
- Keywords: zero-shot, few-shot, examples, demonstration.
- Justification: core prompting distinction the brief must differentiate.

1.3 Chain-of-thought prompting
- Concept: eliciting step-by-step reasoning before the answer.
- Sources: S3 (and S1 where CoT is discussed as a technique).
- Keywords: chain-of-thought, reasoning, step-by-step, scratchpad.
- Justification: required coverage; tie to agent reasoning.

1.4 ReAct
- Concept: interleaving reasoning and acting (tool use) in a loop.
- Sources: S1 (Chip Huyen Agents, describes ReAct patterns).
- Keywords: ReAct, reasoning, acting, tools, loop, Yao.
- Justification: required coverage; bridges prompting and agents.

SECTION 2 — RETRIEVAL AND RAG
2.1 Embeddings
- Concept: numerical vector representations of text enabling similarity.
- Sources: S4 (advanced retrieval), S1.
- Keywords: embeddings, vector, semantic similarity, representation.
- Justification: required coverage; basis of vector search.

2.2 Vector search / vector stores
- Concept: storing and querying embeddings for nearest-neighbor retrieval.
- Sources: S4, S1.
- Keywords: vector store, vector database, similarity search, index, Chroma.
- Justification: required coverage.

2.3 Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
- Concept: retrieving external context and injecting it into generation.
- Sources: S4, S1.
- Keywords: RAG, retrieval, generation, grounding, context.
- Justification: required coverage; central workflow.

2.4 ChromaDB
- Concept: the vector database used to store/query embeddings.
- Sources: S4 (explicitly names ChromaDB).
- Keywords: ChromaDB, collection, query, vector database.
- Justification: required coverage; concrete implementation.

2.5 How retrieval supplies context to generation
- Concept: retrieved passages become prompt context for grounded answers.
- Sources: S4, S1, S2 (research system uses retrieval).
- Keywords: context injection, grounding, search results, generation.
- Justification: connects retrieval to the prompting/generation pipeline.

SECTION 3 — AGENT SYSTEMS
3.1 Orchestration
- Concept: coordinating model calls, tools, and flow across a system.
- Sources: S2 (multi-agent orchestration), S1.
- Keywords: orchestration, coordinator, workflow, pipeline.
- Justification: required coverage.

3.2 Multi-agent execution
- Concept: multiple specialized agents cooperating on sub-tasks.
- Sources: S2 (Anthropic research system), S1.
- Keywords: multi-agent, subagents, delegation, parallel.
- Justification: required coverage.

3.3 Agent memory
- Concept: storing state/context across agent turns.
- Sources: S1 (agent memory), S2.
- Keywords: memory, context, state, short-term, long-term.
- Justification: required coverage.

3.4 Function calling / tool use
- Concept: model emitting structured calls to external tools/functions.
- Sources: S1, S2.
- Keywords: function calling, tools, tool use, API calls.
- Justification: required coverage; core agent primitive.

3.5 Error handling with retries / recovery
- Concept: handling tool failures and recovering from errors.
- Sources: S1, S2.
- Keywords: error handling, retries, recovery, fallback, failures.
- Justification: required coverage; reliability of agent systems.

SECTION 4 — SOURCE GAPS
- Explicitly flag any requested concept not substantively explained by the five references (e.g., if ChromaDB or embeddings only appear as keyword mentions without explanation, or if retry mechanisms are asserted without detail). Cite per concept and state "source gap" rather than filling from memory.

WORD/DISCIPLINE CONSTRAINTS
- 24-80 words per concept or tightly related concept pair; cite source ID in every explanation.
- Sections: Prompting, Retrieval and RAG, Agent Systems, Source Gaps.
- Full brief 600-2,200 words excluding Sources section; avoid fixed numeric recommendations not present in references.

Sources disponibles (identifiant - sujet) :
- [S1] chain-of-thought prompting step-by-step reasoning scratchpad model performance complex tasks agents
- [S2] system developer user message roles differences openai text generation api structured prompting context setting
- [S3] embeddings numerical vector representation semantic similarity text retrieval rag vector search fundamentals
- [S4] zero-shot few-shot prompting examples demonstrations model output steering text generation techniques
- [S5] vector store vector database similarity search index chromadb collection query nearest neighbor retrieval
- [S6] react pattern reasoning acting tool use loop agent architecture yao interleaving thought action
- [S7] rag retrieval-augmented generation context injection grounded answers orchestration multi-agent subagents memory function calling tool use error handling retries recovery
